info.bio: En 1981, el vocalista Ian Astbury se unió a una banda local como la voz principal y la renombró a "Southern Death Cult", en honor a una tribu norteamericana del delta del Mississippi de los siglos XIV y XV. La primera actuación de la banda fue en Queen's Hall en Bradford, Inglaterra el 29 de octubre de 1981. La banda estuvo junta por aproximadamente 16 meses, lanzando un sencillo, "Moya", y tocando con las bandas Bauhaus y Theatre of Hate antes de separarse después de un concierto en Manchester en febrero de 1983.

scenes.name: Gótico
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Término que Hannett aplicó a Joy Division y luego insulto para los epígonos, hasta que en 1982 los fans lo adoptan como estandarte frente a la excesiva luminosidad del new pop: glamour sepulcral, retorno de lo reprimido, emociones atemporales. Bauhaus («Bela Lugosi's Dead», 1979, el comienzo propiamente dicho; Peter Murphy, sex symbol heredero de Adam Ant y Bowie), The Birthday Party (el gótico americano de Nick Cave: «Release the Bats», Junkyard), Killing Joke («música de tensión», del funk de PiL a Black Sabbath, con un aura inquietante), The Cure (gótico light: Seventeen Seconds, Faith, Pornography). El club The Batcave (1982), el «positive punk», Southern Death Cult, Theatre of Hate, The Sisters of Mercy («¡Nosotros sí somos una banda de rock!»), el death rock de Los Ángeles y Kukl con Björk. Su deriva: coqueteos totalitarios y la conversión en versión postpunk del heavy metal (The Cult).

podcast.title: Astbury's Band (1983-1984)
podcast.body: An Ian Astbury-led band mentioned as one of the many groups contributing to the expanding goth scene in the 1983-1984 period. It later evolved into Death Cult and then The Cult. "In Asperg band, Southern Death Cult."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Evolution
podcast.body: The band underwent a name change, first shortening it to Death Cult, and then eventually becoming The Cult. "They started pretty Goth, then they shortened their name to just Death Cult. And finally they just became the cult."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tours with Bauhaus
podcast.body: Southern Death Cult frequently toured with Bauhaus. "It's a band called Southern Death Cult, who often toured with Bauhaus and featured a singer who spent much of his time growing up in Southern Ontario."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Name Evolution
xref.body: Before settling on "The Cult," the band went by two other names: Southern Death Cult (for one album) and Death Cult (for another). By the end of 1983, they were simply "The Cult." "Up until that record came out, The Cult went by two other names."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Evolution from Southern Death Cult
xref.body: The band was initially known as Southern Death Cult, then became Death Cult, and by 1985, they were simply The Cult, showing a progression in their identity. "First they were Southern death cult. Then they became just death cult. By 1985 they were just the cults"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Later Commercial Success
xref.body: After their evolution from Southern Death Cult and Death Cult, The Cult achieved significant commercial success, selling millions of records in the late 1980s and early 1990s. "And yes, it is the cult that went on to sell millions of records in the late 80s and early 1990s."
